definitions.explanation: The part of speech covering words such as ああ, おい, and はい, which stand alone and express feeling, call to someone, or answer. One of the categories used in Japanese school grammar.

examples.japanese: 「ああ」は{感動詞|かんどうし}だ。
{感動詞|かんどうし}は{一語|いちご}で{文|ぶん}になることがある。
examples.english: An interjection can form a sentence all by itself.

examples.japanese: {感動詞|かんどうし}は{活用|かつよう}せず、ほかの{語|ご}を{修飾|しゅうしょく}することもない。
examples.english: Interjections do not conjugate, nor do they modify other words.

notes:
A term from Japanese school grammar. Also called {間投詞|かんとうし}, which is the label more usual in linguistics and in dictionaries of European languages.

TYPICAL MEMBERS:
- {感動|かんどう}: ああ, おお, まあ — expressing feeling
- {呼|よ}びかけ: おい, ねえ, もしもし — calling to someone
- {応答|おうとう}: はい, いいえ, うん — answering

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {助詞|じょし}: particle — attaches to other words; an interjection stands alone
- {副詞|ふくし}: adverb — modifies a predicate, which an interjection never does
